title: Setting a conduit's rate limits to zero keeps an Instance registered as Active while rendering it operationally inert
content:
The Avalanche instance at A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.1.1.2.4.1 and .4.2 records inflow `maxAmount: 0`, `slope: 0` and outflow `maxAmount: 0`, `slope: 0` — yet it is filed under a parent stating that instances "with `Active` Status are stored herein."

With both the ceiling and the refill rate at zero, the leaky bucket never fills: no capital can move in either direction. The instance is fully specified, contract addresses published, processes defined — and completely unusable.

This reveals two independent levers rather than one. `Status` describes whether an integration is *sanctioned and maintained*; rate limits describe whether it is *funded*. Separating them lets governance pre-approve and pre-audit a venue in advance of allocating to it, and lets an operator throttle a live venue to a standstill without deregistering it or losing the reviewed configuration.

The practical implication for anyone reading the Artifact: `Active` is not evidence of activity. Judging Spark's real exposure requires reading the rate limits, not the status headings — an easy misreading given how the document is organized.
description: The Avalanche Aave-type conduit sits under Active Status with maxAmount 0 and slope 0 on both inflow and outflow — deployment status and usable capacity are decoupled controls.
